visualization.help:
# What is R (webR)?
R (webR) runs **R 4.6** in your browser with [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/), and installs packages from **Bioconductor's webR repository** and **CRAN's webR repository**. Nothing runs on the Galaxy server.
## Key Features
- **Script and console**: Write a script, run it whole or line by line (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter), or type into the console. - **Your dataset**: The dataset you opened is in the R session; its path is in `galaxy_input`. - **Plots and files**: Plots and files you create can be downloaded or sent to your history. - **Packages**: Install CRAN and Bioconductor packages from the Packages tab, or with `install.packages()`. - **Saved scripts**: Save the script with the visualization and it comes back when you reopen it.
## Limits
- Running code cannot be interrupted; **Restart R** stops it and clears the session. - R has about 2 GB of memory and one core. - Only packages with webR builds can be installed. Some Bioconductor packages, including DESeq2 and edgeR, cannot be installed yet. - Packages that need the internet at run time (AnnotationHub, biomaRt) or other programs (Python, pandoc) do not work.
webR and R are licensed under the GNU GPL; see `webr/LICENSE.md` in this visualization.
